02 Aug 2026 · Polar Diffusion

Some ideas for the paper

Improved-diffusion Imagenet64

schedule: cosine; T: 4000;

Baseline FID: 22.45

Ours (DDPM sample):

Indepdenet Flow Matching

\[\begin{equation} r_t = (1-t)r_0 + tr_1\quad \text{where} \quad r_0 \sim N(0,1) \end{equation}\] \[\begin{equation} x_t = SLERP(x_0, x_1, t) \quad \text{where} \quad x_0 \sim N(0,1) \end{equation}\]

r_1, x_1 from same y_1

Training algorithm

  • Sample t $\in [0,1]$
  • Sample $y_1$ from data and get $x_1$, $r_1$.
  • Sample $y_0$ from Gaussian and get $x_0$, $r_0$
  • Calculate $x_t$, $r_t$.
  • Get $v^r_t$ from $dr_t/dt$ and $v^x_t$ from $dx_t/dt$
  • L = \(w_x \|v_\theta^x(x_t, r_t, t) -v^x_t\|^2_2+w_r\|v_\theta^r(x_t, r_t, t) -v^r_t\|^2_2\)

Sampling algorithm

  • Sample $y_0$ from Gaussian
  • Get $x_0$, $r_0$ from $y_0$
  • $\Delta=1/T$
  • For $ t =0, 1, 2, \dots, T-1$
    • $x_{t+1} = Exp_{x_t}(v_\theta^x(x_t, r_t, t)\Delta)$
    • $r_{t+1} = r_t + v_\theta^r(x_t, r_t, t)\Delta$
  • $y_1 = r_1x_1$

r_1, x_1 from different y_1. r_1 is a normal distribution, x_1 is also a normal distribution

Training algorithm

  • Sample t $\in [0,1]$
  • Sample $y_1$ from data and get $x_1$, $r_1$.
  • Sample $x_0$ from Unif(S) and $r_0$ from Gaussian.
  • Calculate $x_t$, $r_t$.
  • Get $v^r_t$ from $dr_t/dt$ and $v^x_t$ from $dx_t/dt$
  • L = \(w_x \|v_\theta^x(x_t, r_t, t) -v^x_t\|^2_2+w_r\|v_\theta^r(x_t, r_t, t) -v^r_t\|^2_2\)

Sampling algorithm

  • Sample $x_0$ from Unif(S) and $r_0$ from Gaussian.
  • $\Delta = 1 / T$
  • For $t = 0, 1, 2, \dots, T-1$
    • $x_{t+1} = Exp_{x_t}(v_\theta^x(x_t, r_t, t)\Delta)$
    • $r_{t+1} = r_t + v_\theta^r(x_t, r_t, t)\Delta$
  • $y_1 = r_1x_1$
